not_set_up: Whereabouts is not set up. Add it under Settings → Devices & services.
card_off: This card is switched off in the Whereabouts options (Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure).
forbidden: You are not allowed to see this history.
no_history_persons: No history to show. Choose the persons to record under Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure.
ed_height_auto: Automatic (full height in a panel view)
ed_persons_help: Applies to this card only and wins. Empty = your choice in the Whereabouts settings (Whereabouts dashboard → Settings).
ed_picture_help: e.g. /local/pictures/alex.jpg (folder www in the configuration directory). Empty = the person's picture from Home Assistant.
ed_map_link_choice: On phones and tablets ask which app
ed_map_link_choice_help: A tap on the coordinates shows a choice of map apps (e.g. Apple Maps, Google Maps, Waze). The app chosen above comes first.
ed_similar_colors: Hard to tell apart – similar colours: {pairs}. Choose a clearly different colour for one of them.
settings_failed: The settings could not be loaded.
scope_own_text: These settings apply only to you – in the Whereabouts dashboard and in the Whereabouts cards of your dashboards. Switches and selections save at once, text and number fields with "Save" or the Enter key.
scope_defaults_text: Here you set what every user starts with. Users who changed nothing themselves, or for whom a category is locked, get these values. Users' own settings are kept.
confirm_reset_category: Everything in "{name}" goes back to the built-in values of Whereabouts. For 30 seconds you can restore your values afterwards.
confirm_reset_defaults: The default values in "{name}" are set back to Whereabouts' own values. This affects every user who set nothing there themselves.
confirm_reset_all: All your personal settings are deleted. The default values apply everywhere again.
lock_text: Whoever the category is fixed for sees it greyed out with the default for all users and cannot change it. Their own values stay stored and apply again as soon as it is released.
cd_views: Which views the Whereabouts dashboard shows and which one it starts with.
cd_persons: Who appears in the maps, in which order, with which name, colour and picture.
cd_map: Look of the map and where a tap on coordinates leads.
cd_zones: Zones of Home Assistant as circles in the maps – where, in which colours and which ones.
cd_live: Info bar, status bar, automatic refresh and behaviour of the live map.
cd_history: Start view and period, legend, export button, points and automatic refresh.
cd_rights: What other users may see and delete and with which settings they work.
cd_sidebar: Whether Whereabouts appears as a dashboard in the sidebar, with which name and which icon.
cd_recording: Whose history is stored, how fine and how long.
cd_addresses: Where the address comes from when somebody is not in a zone.
cd_data: Download location data or take it over from a file.
cd_diagnostics: Trackers, address sensor and stored history per person – helps when something is missing.
si_view_live: Shows the tab with the live map.
si_view_history: Shows the tab with the history.
si_view_settings:
**Off:** the view disappears from the dashboard.

**Still reachable:** at /whereabouts/settings, under Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure → Open settings and – for administrators – with the gear in the maps.
si_start_view: Which view appears when the dashboard is opened. If it is hidden, the first visible one comes.
si_person:
**Tick:** the person appears in the maps.

**Arrows:** the order (also in the info bar).

**Name:** empty = the name from Home Assistant.

**Colour:** of the pin, the route and the name.

**Picture:** drop or choose a picture and crop it (stored small, 256 × 256); "Remove" = the person's picture from Home Assistant.

**Show in:** in which map the person appears – the recording does not depend on it.

**Good to know:** uploaded pictures are kept by Home Assistant like person pictures and can be opened with their random address without signing in. Only persons you may see can be chosen.
upload_failed: The picture could not be uploaded.
no_persons_allowed: You may not see any persons. The administrator decides this.
si_map_style: "Like Home Assistant" follows the light/dark mode of your theme.
si_tiles: Esri and OpenStreetMap need no key. CARTO needs a free key that the administrator enters once for everybody; which CARTO style each map shows is set below it. If a provider delivers no map at all any more (e.g. key blocked), the map switches by itself: CARTO → Esri → OpenStreetMap. Your browser loads the tiles directly from the provider.
si_map_link: Which map opens when nobody is asked: on a computer always, on phones and tablets when "ask for the app" is off. "Nothing" shows the coordinates without a link.
st_map_link_choice: On phones and tablets ask which app
si_map_link_choice:
**On:** a tap on coordinates on a phone or tablet shows a choice of map apps (below).

**Off:** the preferred map opens directly.

**On a computer:** always the preferred map.
si_zone_color_home: Colour of the circle of the zone Home.
si_zone_color: Colour of the circles of all other zones.
si_zone_names_zoom: Below it only the circles are shown so the map is not cluttered. 1 = whole world, 20 = single houses.
si_show_info_bar: The tiles at the top of the map with picture, place, since when and last fix. A tap jumps to the person.
si_show_status_bar: The bar at the bottom with the coordinates, the time of the last update and the reload button.
st_show_accuracy: GPS accuracy circle on the way
si_show_accuracy: A light circle shows how exact the fix is. Circles above 1 km are not drawn.
si_follow: The map shows all persons and moves along when they are on the way. As soon as you move or zoom the map, this stops – until you press the overview button at the bottom right (above the zoom buttons).
si_live_refresh_interval: How often the map refreshes automatically (default 30 seconds). Only used while “Refresh automatically” is on.
si_default_view: What the location history opens with and where "Today" returns to. You can switch at any time at the top of the view.
si_show_legend: Bottom left: colours of the persons, the symbols for start and end and the switch "Show zones".
si_show_export: The button “Export data” at the bottom left of the history card: a day or a period, persons, CSV, GPX or a map picture (JPG).
si_history_refresh_interval: How often the history refreshes automatically (default 30 seconds). Not while an entry is open or multiple selection is active. Only used while “Refresh automatically” is on.
admin_all: Administrator – sees and may do everything.
rights_by_admin: Your rights are set by the administrator.
si_rights_default_live: Applies to every user without own rights. Note: this only affects what Whereabouts shows. Every logged-in user can in principle also see the persons' positions elsewhere in Home Assistant (e.g. on the normal map) – no integration can prevent that.
si_rights_default_history: Applies to every user without own rights. The history is really protected: Whereabouts hands it out only to users who may see it. "Own person" = the person linked to the user account (Settings → People).
si_rights_default_delete: Applies to every user without own rights. Default for new installations: nobody – only administrators delete. Deleting only works for persons whose history the user may see, too.
confirm_rights_less: Users without own rights will see or may do less than before. Continue?
confirm_rights_rules: The rules for everybody apply to {user} again; the own rights are deleted.
si_panel_title: Empty = "Standorte" or "Whereabouts" depending on the system language of Home Assistant (shown greyed in the field). Home Assistant knows only one name for all users.
si_panel_icon: An icon from Material Design Icons, e.g. mdi:map-marker-radius. Empty = the default icon.
si_live_card: Off: the live map exists for nobody – neither as a tab nor in dashboards.
si_show_persons_live: Who can appear in the live map at all. Every user sees only those of them they may see.
si_history_card: Off: the history card exists for nobody and nothing is recorded.
si_show_persons_history: Whose history can be shown at all. Hiding does not delete any history.
si_carto_api_key: “Get a key” sends it to you by e-mail for free (enter your e-mail, your Home Assistant's domain and a short purpose; no CARTO account needed). Enter only the value “Your API key” (starts with cb1_…) – the URLs from the e-mail are not needed. If you paste a whole URL anyway, Whereabouts takes the key from it. After saving, Whereabouts checks once whether CARTO accepts the key. The key goes to every user's browser (they load the tiles with it), so it is not a secret.
st_record_persons: Record the history of these persons
si_record_persons:
**Ticked:** the history of this person is recorded from now on. Nothing is recorded until persons are ticked here.

**Taking out:** recording stops, the history so far stays.

**Independent of the display:** whether a person appears in the maps is set under Persons.

**Where the data are:** only on this Home Assistant (folder whereabouts in the configuration folder), part of every backup.

**Tip:** a person can have several trackers (Companion app and e.g. a router tracker for the home network) – assign them in Home Assistant under Settings → People.
st_min_interval: At the same place store at most every … seconds
si_min_interval:
**Change of place:** entering or leaving a zone is always stored at once.

**At the same place:** frequent updates are thinned out to this interval.
si_same_place_distance:
**On the way:** positions closer together than this count as one stay.

**In a zone:** the exact position does not matter.

**Larger – smaller:** larger joins more, smaller keeps more single places.
si_retention_days:
**0:** nothing is ever deleted automatically (standard).

**More than 0:** every night at 3:17 all days that are older are deleted – for all persons and irreversibly.

**Good to know:** this also concerns imported days.
confirm_retention: From tonight every day older than {n} days is deleted – for all persons and irreversibly. Really switch on?
si_address_source:
**Companion app:** the address the Home Assistant app on the phone already determined – stays local. Switch on the sensor "Geocoded location" in the app (App settings → Companion app → Manage sensors).

**OpenStreetMap:** only when the phone's address is missing or does not fit; then the coordinates of the place go to nominatim.openstreetmap.org.

**How it works:** first the phone; its position must be close enough; Whereabouts waits a moment for a new address; otherwise OpenStreetMap. In zones no address is looked up. Addresses found once are kept.
st_address_max_distance: Use the phone's address only up to … metres
si_address_max_distance:
**Why:** the phone does not determine the address for every position anew – its address belongs to where it last looked.

**Further away:** the address is outdated, OpenStreetMap is asked instead.

**Smaller – larger:** smaller is more exact but asks OpenStreetMap more often; larger asks less often but sometimes gives the next street.
si_address_sensor: “Automatic” = the Companion app's sensor “Geocoded location” on the person's device. Only sensors that deliver addresses are listed. Change it only if the one found automatically is wrong.
si_export: Opens the export window: a day or a period, persons (preselected: all whose history you may see), CSV (table, can be imported again) or GPX (for map apps); several files come as a ZIP.

drop_file: Drop a file here or click (CSV, GPX, ZIP – max. 50 MB)
confirm_import: Import now? Existing entries are kept.
confirm_import_replace: Attention: all days that appear in the file are deleted first and replaced by the file – irreversibly.
import_error_unknown_format: The file format was not recognised.
import_error_unreadable: The file could not be read.
import_error_too_large: The file is too large (max. 50 MB, ZIP content max. 200 MB).
import_error_no_points: The file contains no usable entries.
import_error_person_required: Please choose above whom the file belongs to.
import_error_unknown_person: The file names a person that does not exist in Home Assistant. Please choose the person above.

Off: the bottom line shows how current the data is instead (e.g. “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday 14:05”); the button still refreshes on click. New positions from Home Assistant arrive at once either way.
si_history_auto_refresh: On: the history refreshes at the set interval, the ring around the button at the bottom right shows when. Off: the bottom line shows how current the data is instead (e.g. “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday 14:05”); the button still refreshes on click.
download_zip: This makes {n} files – they come together as a ZIP.
editing_defaults: You are editing the standard for all users.

settings_managed: The settings are managed by the administrator.

leave_text: These fields are not saved yet:

carto_key_invalid: This does not look like a CARTO key.
confirm_carto_remove: Without a key, all maps with the CARTO style show Esri again. Remove it?
si_zone_list:
**Tick:** the zone is drawn. New zones appear by themselves.

**Own colour:** replaces the colour above for this zone.

**Good to know:** this is only the display – the recording still knows all zones.
cd_base: Which persons (not users) from Home Assistant Whereabouts knows at all. Only they can be chosen in all other settings: persons, rights, recording, addresses and import.
si_persons:
**Ticked:** the person exists for Whereabouts. All ticked = new persons in Home Assistant come along by themselves.

**Not ticked:** the person appears nowhere in Whereabouts and is not recorded; their history stays.

**Good to know:** a family member without a phone can stay out, so nobody has to tick them off everywhere.
base_needs_one: At least one person must stay ticked.
si_show_technical: Users who may only log in locally or belong to no person – e.g. the MQTT broker's user. They are normally hidden.
address_auto_missing: No sensor found – OpenStreetMap is used. Switch on "Geocoded location" in the Companion app.
si_import_person: “As given in the file”: the person is in the file (column person). Otherwise every entry of the file belongs to the chosen person – needed for GPX, which knows no person.
si_import_replace: Off: entries that already exist are skipped, everything else is added. On: every day in the file is deleted first and replaced by the file – irreversibly.
format_help: What must the file look like?
format_help_csv: CSV (UTF-8, first row column names, separator comma or semicolon). One row is one stay:
format_col_person: person: the part after “person.” (e.g. alex for person.alex)
format_col_time: start, end: time HH:MM:SS, local time; end may be empty
format_col_state: state: home, not_home or the name of a zone
format_col_coords: latitude, longitude: degrees with a point (e.g. 48.7784)
format_help_gpx: GPX: tracks, routes and waypoints with a time. Choose the person above under “Belongs to”.
format_help_zip: ZIP: many CSV files at once, also the daily files of the original script version (<person>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv).
ai_help: Have data from another app converted
ai_help_text: Copy this text into an AI assistant and attach the other app's file. The result is a CSV for the import.
ai_privacy: Location data is very personal: whoever gives it to an online service gives it away. Only upload data that you and the person concerned agree to – or use an AI assistant that runs on your own device.
ai_prompt:
Convert the attached location data into a CSV file for the Home Assistant integration “Whereabouts”.

Target format (UTF-8, comma as separator, first row exactly like this):
person,date,start,end,state,latitude,longitude,address

Rules:
1. person: always PERSON (replace PERSON beforehand with the name without “person.”, only lower-case letters, digits and _).
2. One row per stay. Merge consecutive points at the same place into one row: start = first, end = last time there.
3. date as YYYY-MM-DD, start and end as HH:MM:SS, all in local time (not UTC). If a stay crosses midnight, split it at the end of the day and continue the next day at 00:00:00.
4. state: home only if it is certain that it is the home; the name of a zone only if it is known; otherwise not_home.
5. latitude and longitude in decimal degrees with a point, at least 5 decimal places.
6. address only for not_home and only if it is in the data; otherwise leave it empty. Put values containing a comma in quotes.
7. Output only the content of the CSV, without explanations.
8. If something is unclear (time zone, home, zones), ask instead of guessing.
copy_manually: Copying did not work – the text is selected, please copy it yourself.
pick_end: Now choose the end of the period (or Choose for this day).
large_period_warning: Long period: loading takes longer and puts load on Home Assistant. The data is fetched month by month.
image_hint: The picture shows the map as it is set right now (period, persons, route or heatmap).
image_failed: The map picture could not be made.
image_blocked: The map tiles could not be loaded for the picture – the map service cannot be reached right now or does not allow map pictures. Try another map style.
si_carto_live_light: Which CARTO style the live map shows in light mode. Voyager is colourful and easy to read, Positron light grey and calm, Dark Matter dark. “Without labels” leaves out street and place names.
si_carto_live_dark: Which CARTO style the live map shows in dark mode.
si_carto_history_light: Which CARTO style the history shows in light mode. Positron makes the coloured routes stand out.
si_carto_history_dark: Which CARTO style the history shows in dark mode.
si_zones_in: In which map the zones from Home Assistant (except passive ones) appear as circles with names. The switch "Show zones" in the legend of the location history changes the same setting.
scope_user_text: You are editing this user's settings. The lock next to a setting fixes it for them: they see it greyed out with your value and cannot change it.
editing_user: You are editing the settings of {name}.
editing_user_synced: {name} is synchronised with your settings – changes here apply only once that is off.
confirm_reset_user: The settings of {user} in "{name}" go back to the built-in values of Whereabouts. For 30 seconds you can restore them afterwards.
confirm_reset_options: Everything in “{name}” goes back to Whereabouts' values.
success_make_default: "{name}" is now the standard for all users.
success_sync_all_on: Synchronisation is on – your settings now apply to all users.
success_sync_all_off: Synchronisation is off – your settings are now the default for all users.
success_sync_user_on: {name} is now synchronised with your settings.
success_sync_user_off: Synchronisation for {name} is off – your settings are now {name}'s own.
confirm_sync_all_on: From now on your settings apply to every user who is not an administrator – new ones too. Their “Settings” tab disappears.
confirm_sync_all_off: Your settings become the default for all users. The users' own settings are deleted – this cannot be undone. Administrators, rights and fixed settings stay as they are.
confirm_sync_user_on: From now on your settings apply to {name}, continuously. The “Settings” tab disappears for {name}.
confirm_sync_user_off: {name} keeps your current settings as their own and can change them again afterwards (if you show the “Settings” tab).
field_free: {name} may change this – click to fix it
import_intro: Take over history from a file.
si_import_mode: Merge: per day only entries that fall into a gap are added – a time for which there is no stay yet. Nothing is stored twice, nothing existing is overwritten. Skip: days that already have data stay untouched; only days without data are taken. Replace: every day in the file is deleted first and replaced by the file – irreversibly. In every case a window shows beforehand what happens per day, and you choose the days.
import_summary: {n} new {n|entry|entries} on {days} {days|day|days} chosen · {none} {none|day|days} with nothing new
lock_explain_users: Single settings you fix for one user under Users → Edit.
points_hidden: {n} points hidden · zoom in to show them
zones_switch_card: Fixed in this card's settings – changed only until you leave
ed_start_period_help: Which period the history shows when opened; "Today" (clicked a second time) returns to it.
ed_simplify_points_help: With many entries the small points of the route only appear when zoomed in. 0 = always show.
si_start_period:
**Opening:** the history starts with this period.

**"Today":** the first click shows only today, a second click goes back to the start view and this period.
si_simplify_points:
**Why:** with many entries (e.g. several weeks) the small points of the route cover the map and make it slow.

**Hidden:** from this number of entries on, only the line, start and end are drawn; a note at the top of the map says how many points are hidden.

**Zooming in:** close up the points appear again – or click the note. 0 = always show points. Only for the route, not for the heat map.
si_map_link_apps:
**To choose from:** these map apps appear when you tap coordinates on a phone or tablet.

**Fitting the device:** Apple Maps is never offered on Android.

**Only one app left:** it opens directly, without asking.
apps_need_one: At least one app must stay chosen.
zone_list_intro: Which zones are drawn and in which colour.
contrast_light: Hard to see on the light map – please choose a darker or stronger colour.
contrast_dark: Hard to see on the dark map – please choose a lighter colour.
contrast_both: Hard to see on the light and on the dark map – please choose a stronger colour.
restore_title: Undo going back to the standard
all_standard: Everything here is at the standard.
person_standard: name, colour and picture from Home Assistant
marker_explain: A blue dot marks an own value (standard would be shown on hover); the arrow next to it goes back to the standard – for 30 seconds "Restore" brings your value back. "Reset to standard" sets a whole area to the built-in values.
scope_own_text_single: These settings apply to the Whereabouts dashboard and to the Whereabouts cards in your dashboards. Switches and selections save at once, text and number fields with "Save" or the Enter key.
single_user_hint: With two or more users there are more options: settings per user, a standard for everybody, fixing settings for users and rights for each user. They appear here as soon as there is another user (not an administrator).
reset_for_everyone: Also reset for all users (their own values and the standard)
confirm_hide_settings: The view "Settings" disappears from the dashboard. You can still reach it at /whereabouts/settings.
confirm_hide_settings_admin: The view "Settings" disappears from the dashboard. Ways back: the gear in both maps (only for administrators), /whereabouts/settings, or Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure → Open settings.
si_panel_hidden:
**On:** the dashboard disappears from the sidebar – for everybody. The cards in other dashboards keep working.

**How to get there anyway:** the gear in the maps (administrators), Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure → Open settings, or the address /whereabouts.

**Hide only for yourself:** Profile → Edit sidebar (or press and hold the sidebar).
confirm_hide_panel: The Whereabouts dashboard disappears from the sidebar for everybody. Ways back: the gear in the maps (administrators), /whereabouts, or Settings → Devices & services → Whereabouts → Configure → Open settings.
cd_rights_self: Whose position you see live and whose history you may see and delete.
si_users_table:
**All users (standard):** the rules for everybody without own rights, and the standard settings ("Edit").

**Own rights:** tick it for a user to choose persons one by one; without it the rules apply.

**Settings:** "View Settings" shows or hides the settings for the user; "Sync with me" gives them your settings all the time (when switched off they keep them as their own). "Edit" changes the user's settings and can fix single ones.

**Good to know:** rights only concern Whereabouts – every signed-in user can see positions elsewhere in Home Assistant (e.g. the normal map). The history, however, is really protected.
admins_see_all: Administrators always see everything and may delete everything; their settings are their own.
edit_synced: Synchronised with an administrator – switch that off first
new_users_later: Later (until then like my settings, I will be asked again)
new_users_rights: Rights (pre-set with the rules for all users):
new_users_later_done: Rights saved – you will be asked about the settings next time.
confirm_retention_count: From tonight on every day older than {n} days is deleted – for all persons and irreversibly. Tonight {files} day files disappear. Really switch it on?
sensors_intro: Per recorded person the phone's sensor "Geocoded location" – found automatically.
si_sensors:
**Automatically:** Whereabouts takes the sensor of the Companion app on the person's phone.

**Other choice:** replaces the automatic one (blue dot; the arrow goes back to automatic).

**No sensor:** for that person OpenStreetMap is used.
si_address_sensor_for: Which sensor delivers the address of {name}.
picture_from_web_text: Address of a picture (https://…). Home Assistant loads it once (at most 10 MB); only the small cropped picture is stored.
picture_load_failed: The picture could not be loaded.
picture_bad_url: Please enter an address starting with https://
picture_error_too_large: The picture is larger than 10 MB.
picture_error_not_public: Only addresses on the internet are possible (not in the home network).
picture_error_invalid_url: That is not a valid address.
picture_error_unreachable: The address could not be reached.
picture_crop_text: Move the picture and zoom so that the face sits in the circle.
